stem: Two unaffected parents are each known carriers of the same pathogenic variant for an autosomal recessive disorder. What is the probability that their next child will inherit the disorder?

options.label: A
options.misconception: Carrier probability is being confused with affected-child probability.
options.explanation: Half of children are expected to be carriers, while one quarter are expected to be affected.

options.label: B
options.misconception: All children inheriting at least one variant are being counted as affected.
options.explanation: Carriers have one functional allele and are not affected in a fully penetrant recessive model.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Carrier parents are being treated as if both always transmit the pathogenic allele.
options.explanation: Each parent transmits either allele independently, so affected inheritance is not certain.

options.label: D
options.misconception: The parents' unaffected status is being mistaken for absence of transmissible variants.
options.explanation: Unaffected carriers can each transmit the pathogenic allele, creating a one-in-four affected risk.

options.label: E
options.misconception: None; two heterozygous parents produce an affected homozygous genotype in one quarter of conceptions.
options.explanation: An Aa by Aa cross yields AA, Aa, Aa, and aa in equal quarter-probabilities; only aa is affected.

context: Learning objective: calculate recurrence risk for an autosomal recessive condition. Each carrier has a one-half chance of transmitting the pathogenic allele; the independent joint probability is one-half multiplied by one-half, or one quarter, for every pregnancy.
